title: Dynamic Web Programming - Midterm Unique 60 Questions

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture's completed fetch example, which JavaScript expression creates a new image element equivalent to `document.createElement('img')`?

options.text: `document.newImage()`
`image.create()`
`new Img()`
`new Image()`

questions.explanationMd: `new Image()` creates an HTML image element, similar to creating an `` element with `document.createElement('img')`.

questions.questionMd: Which command is used to serve local files over HTTP so that `fetch()` can access them during development?

options.text: `python3 -m http.server`
`python3 -m fetch-server`
`npm start http`
`node server.js`

questions.explanationMd: `python3 -m http.server` starts a simple local HTTP server, avoiding browser restrictions that can occur with `file://` URLs.

questions.questionMd: Which HTTP method does a browser send automatically whenever you navigate to a URL in the address bar?

options.text: DELETE
PUT
POST
GET

questions.explanationMd: Normal browser navigation sends an HTTP `GET` request to retrieve the resource at the entered URL.

questions.questionMd: What is the key difference between calling `response.text()` and `response.json()` inside a `fetch()` response handler?

options.text: `response.text()` returns a Promise while `response.json()` returns a value directly
`response.json()` automatically parses the response string into a JavaScript object
`response.text()` is faster because it skips validation
`response.json()` only works with REST APIs, not local files

questions.explanationMd: Both methods are asynchronous, but `response.json()` parses the body as JSON and resolves to the resulting JavaScript value.

questions.questionMd: How does the lecture describe XMLHttpRequest (XHR) compared to the Fetch API?

options.text: Simpler but less flexible
Clunky and harder to use
More secure and widely supported
Faster and more reliable

questions.explanationMd: XHR is the older request API and is usually considered more verbose and harder to use than the Promise-based Fetch API.

questions.questionMd: In JavaScript, how do you read the current text entered by a user in an `<input type="text">` element?

options.text: `inputElement.innerHTML`
`inputElement.value`
`inputElement.textContent`
`inputElement.data`

questions.explanationMd: For text input elements, the current user-entered value is stored in the element's `.value` property.

questions.questionMd: Which of the following is listed in the lecture as one of the HTTP methods used in RESTful API requests?

options.text: DELETE
QUERY
FETCH
STREAM

questions.explanationMd: RESTful APIs commonly use HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what is the problem with using ordinary inner functions (closures) as callbacks in `fetch().then()` chains inside a class method?

options.text: Closures capture the value of `this` at the time the outer function is defined rather than at the time it is called, leading to a stale reference in long-lived operations
Closures defined inside a method are garbage-collected before the `fetch()` promise resolves, causing a null reference error when the callback eventually fires
Each function has its own `this` value, so closures do not automatically inherit the `this` binding of their enclosing class method
The `fetch()` API enforces strict mode internally, which prevents closures from accessing any variable declared in the outer function scope with the `var` keyword

questions.explanationMd: Ordinary functions have their own `this`, so callbacks passed to `.then()` may not keep the class instance as `this` unless they are bound or arrow functions are used.

questions.questionMd: Which combination of components makes up the Chrome browser's architecture as described in the lecture?

options.text: The SpiderMonkey interpreter, the CSS rendering pipeline, and the WebAssembly execution environment for compiled code modules
The TCP socket library, the DNS resolver module, and the ExpressJS routing engine embedded into the browser at compile time
The V8 JavaScript engine (with parser, execution engine, and garbage collector), the JavaScript runtime, and the DOM API implementation
The npm package manager, the NodeJS API implementation, and a built-in HTTP server for serving static web assets locally

questions.explanationMd: Chrome uses V8 to execute JavaScript, plus browser-provided runtime features and DOM APIs for interacting with web pages.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture's definition, what is a “gotcha” in programming?

options.text: A valid construct that works as documented but is counter-intuitive and almost invites mistakes because it is easy to invoke and unexpected in its outcome
A deprecated API function that still exists in the language specification for backward compatibility but produces incorrect results when called in strict mode environments
A deliberate bug intentionally left in a codebase by a developer to test whether automated testing pipelines are comprehensive enough to catch subtle logic errors
A security vulnerability in a programming language runtime that attackers can exploit to execute arbitrary code by supplying malformed input to a parsing function

questions.explanationMd: A gotcha is behavior that is technically valid but surprising enough that developers commonly make mistakes with it.

questions.questionMd: Which built-in JavaScript array method is used in the lecture to reorder album objects by year?

options.text: `.reduce()`
`.filter()`
`.sort()`

questions.explanationMd: The `.sort()` method reorders array elements, typically using a comparator function for custom ordering.

questions.questionMd: What does CORS stand for?

options.text: Client-Only Resource Serialization, a browser policy that restricts JavaScript from reading binary resources loaded from external CDN servers
Cross-Origin Resource Sharing
Controlled Object Request Standard, an HTTP extension that governs how request headers are validated before the server processes the payload
Cross-Origin Response Security, an encryption layer added to HTTP responses that prevents man-in-the-middle interception of API data in transit

questions.explanationMd: CORS stands for Cross-Origin Resource Sharing, a browser security mechanism for controlled cross-origin requests.

questions.questionMd: Which of the following best describes a RESTful API?

options.text: A protocol for rendering HTML pages dynamically using query strings
An interface that exclusively uses the POST method to exchange data
An API that only works with browser-side JavaScript and cannot be accessed from a server
A URL-based API that uses HTTP methods and sends requests to a base endpoint

questions.explanationMd: RESTful APIs expose resources through URLs and use HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what does TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) define?

options.text: The mapping between domain names and IP addresses maintained by distributed name servers across the internet
The structure and syntax of HTTP request and response messages exchanged between a browser and a web server
The data format used for sending information over the network wire, and it can be used for HTTP, FTP, and other protocols
The encryption standard applied to HTTPS traffic to protect data transmitted between clients and servers

questions.explanationMd: In the lecture framing, TCP is the lower-level transport protocol used underneath application protocols such as HTTP and FTP.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture summary, after the server software receives an HTTP request, what is the correct sequence of actions it takes?

options.text: The server software parses the message, creates an HTTP response, and then the server OS sends that response to the client over TCP
The server software binds to a new port, sends an HTTP GET request back to the client to confirm receipt, then closes the connection
The server software immediately sends an empty 200 OK response and then asynchronously processes the request body in the background
The server software forwards the raw TCP packet to the DNS server, which translates it and routes the reply back to the client browser

questions.explanationMd: A server program reads and parses the incoming request, prepares an HTTP response, and the operating system handles sending it over TCP.

questions.questionMd: Which of the following best describes a JavaScript Promise?

options.text: A synchronous function that immediately returns a value
A built-in timer that delays code execution by a specified amount
An object that handles asynchronous operations
A special array type used to store multiple fetch results

questions.explanationMd: A Promise represents the eventual result of an asynchronous operation, either fulfilled or rejected.

questions.questionMd: Who created JSON?

options.text: Brendan Eich
Tim Berners-Lee
Douglas Crockford
James Gosling

questions.explanationMd: JSON is commonly associated with Douglas Crockford, who popularized and specified the format.

questions.questionMd: What does `JSON.parse()` accept as its argument?

options.text: A fetch response object
A Promise returned by `fetch()`
A JSON-formatted string
A JavaScript object to be serialized

questions.explanationMd: `JSON.parse()` takes a JSON-formatted string and converts it into the corresponding JavaScript value.

questions.questionMd: What is the key difference between the DOM API used in Chrome and the NodeJS API?

options.text: The DOM API handles TCP socket connections and port binding, while the NodeJS API handles HTML parsing and CSS rendering
The DOM API uses the V8 engine for execution while the NodeJS API uses a different interpreter called SpiderMonkey for server tasks
The DOM API is written in JavaScript and runs only on Linux servers, while the NodeJS API is written in C++ and runs inside browsers
The DOM API provides JavaScript libraries to interact with a web page, while the NodeJS API provides libraries useful for creating server programs

questions.explanationMd: The DOM API is browser-oriented for page interaction, while NodeJS provides APIs for server-side tasks such as files, networking, and HTTP servers.

questions.questionMd: Which of the following data types is natively preserved when a JavaScript object is serialized to JSON using `JSON.stringify()`?

options.text: Date objects
`undefined` values
Numbers
Functions

questions.explanationMd: JSON natively represents strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, objects, and null; functions and `undefined` are not preserved as normal values.

questions.questionMd: How does NodeJS handle the complexity of network sockets when building a web server?

options.text: NodeJS uses the V8 engine's built-in socket library to open encrypted connections on all available network ports
NodeJS abstracts socket management away so developers do not need to think about sockets directly
NodeJS requires developers to manually create and bind sockets before attaching any HTTP request listeners
NodeJS delegates all socket creation to the browser's DOM API, which then forwards messages to the server program

questions.explanationMd: NodeJS provides higher-level server APIs so developers can listen for requests without manually managing raw sockets in typical web-server code.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, can NodeJS be used for purposes other than building web servers?

options.text: Yes, NodeJS can be used to write general-purpose JavaScript scripts that are completely unrelated to web servers
Yes, but only if the scripts use the DOM API, because NodeJS was designed as a bridge between browser JavaScript and server JavaScript
No, NodeJS requires an active internet connection at all times and cannot run JavaScript files that make no network requests
No, NodeJS is exclusively designed for server-side HTTP handling and cannot execute scripts that do not involve network connections

questions.explanationMd: NodeJS is a JavaScript runtime that can run many kinds of scripts, not only web servers.

questions.questionMd: When handling a form's `submit` event in JavaScript, what must you call to prevent the page from refreshing?

options.text: `form.reset()`
`window.cancelSubmit()`
`event.stopPropagation()`
`event.preventDefault()`

questions.explanationMd: Calling `event.preventDefault()` stops the browser's default form submission behavior, which normally reloads or navigates the page.

questions.questionMd: Which of the following best describes the “fulfilled” state of a Promise?

options.text: The asynchronous operation completed successfully
The operation encountered a network error
The Promise has been created but not yet started
The Promise is waiting for a `.then()` handler to be attached

questions.explanationMd: A fulfilled Promise is one whose asynchronous operation completed successfully and produced a value.

questions.questionMd: In the discography page example, how does the `SortButton` class communicate a sort action back to the `App` class?

options.text: It fires a built-in DOM click event that the `App` class listens for on the document
It dispatches a custom keyboard event that triggers the App's event listener
It directly modifies the `albumInfo` property of the `App` instance
It calls an `onClickCallback` function passed to it during construction

questions.explanationMd: The `SortButton` receives a callback from the `App` and invokes that callback when a sort action is triggered.

questions.questionMd: In a typical `fetch()` call chain, what does the first `.then()` callback receive as its parameter?

options.text: A Response object from the network request
An array of all fetched resources
The final parsed data ready for use
A JSON string representation of the resource

questions.explanationMd: The first fulfillment handler after `fetch()` receives the `Response` object returned by the network request.

questions.questionMd: Who invented the World Wide Web in 1991 as a way to link research papers using hyperlinks?

options.text: Tim Berners-Lee
Vint Cerf
Steve Jobs
Bill Gates

questions.explanationMd: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web at CERN as a hypertext-based system for linking documents.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, why can multiple images load in parallel even though JavaScript is single-threaded?

options.text: JavaScript uses Web Workers internally for all image element operations, with each Image object spawning its own dedicated worker thread to manage the download lifecycle
The browser batches all image requests into a single multiplexed HTTP/2 stream that the JavaScript engine processes sequentially but displays simultaneously after all bytes arrive
Image loading is handled entirely by the operating system's DNS resolver and network stack, which feeds completed image buffers directly into the browser's graphics memory
The browser itself is multi-threaded and multi-process, so network requests and image decoding happen in browser threads outside the JavaScript runtime

questions.explanationMd: JavaScript execution may be single-threaded, but browsers use separate internal threads and processes for networking, decoding, and rendering work.

questions.questionMd: According to the well-known ports listed in the lecture, which port number is used by the Secure Shell (SSH) protocol?

options.text: Port 23, which is the port number assigned to the Telnet remote login service for unencrypted terminal sessions
Port 22, which is the standard port assigned to the Secure Shell protocol for encrypted remote access
Port 21, which is the port number assigned to the File Transfer Protocol for uploading and downloading files remotely
Port 443, which is the port number reserved for HTTPS and is sometimes mistaken for the SSH port by new developers

questions.explanationMd: SSH uses TCP port 22 by default for encrypted remote shell access.

questions.questionMd: If a NodeJS server is listening on port 3000 of your local machine, which URL would you use in a browser to access it?

options.text: `http://server:3000/local`
`node://localhost:3000`
`http://localhost:3000`

questions.explanationMd: A local web server on port 3000 is normally accessed with `http://localhost:3000`.

questions.questionMd: What is the primary purpose of the `fetch()` function in JavaScript?

options.text: To parse HTML documents and manipulate the DOM
To synchronously read files from the local file system
To load resources asynchronously over a network using a Promise-based approach
To serialize JavaScript objects into JSON strings

questions.explanationMd: `fetch()` is used to make asynchronous network requests and returns a Promise.

questions.questionMd: A developer receives the string `{"name":"Ice Bear"}` from a server. Which function should they use to turn it into a usable JavaScript object?

options.text: `JSON.decode()`
`JSON.parse()`
`JSON.stringify()`
`JSON.objectify()`

questions.explanationMd: `JSON.parse()` converts a JSON-formatted string into a JavaScript object.

questions.questionMd: What is “binding” in the context of running a server process?

options.text: Compiling JavaScript source code into native machine code before the NodeJS runtime begins accepting HTTP requests
Establishing a persistent TCP connection between two servers so they can exchange data without repeating the handshake
Encrypting the server's IP address so that DNS queries return a hashed value instead of the actual numerical address
Telling the operating system which port number to associate with the server process so it can receive incoming messages

questions.explanationMd: Binding associates a server process with a port so the operating system can deliver incoming network messages to it.

questions.questionMd: Why does using `require('express')` in a NodeJS file fail if Express has not been installed first?

options.text: Because the V8 engine blocks third-party module loading until the developer explicitly grants permission through a configuration file
Because `require()` only works with browser-based modules and cannot load server-side libraries like Express into NodeJS
Because Express is not part of the built-in NodeJS API; it must be downloaded separately using npm before it can be required
Because Express requires a valid HTTPS certificate to be present in the project directory before the module can be loaded

questions.explanationMd: Express is a third-party package, so it must be installed with npm before NodeJS can load it using `require('express')`.

questions.questionMd: To allow a form to submit when a user presses the Enter key, which event should be listened for on the `<form>` element?

options.text: keydown
click
submit
change

questions.explanationMd: The form's `submit` event handles both button-based submission and Enter-key submission from form fields.

questions.questionMd: In the completed fetch example, how is each image added to the web page after its URL is extracted?

options.text: A CSS background property is applied to an existing element
The URL is passed to a separate fetch call to load the image data
A new `` element is created and appended to `document.body`
The image URL is written directly into the HTML using `innerHTML`

questions.explanationMd: The example creates an image element, sets its URL, and appends it to the page.

questions.questionMd: What happens when you call `console.log('nodejs')` inside the NodeJS runtime?

options.text: It writes the text to a browser developer tools console by tunneling the output through the V8 engine's debug interface
It throws a ReferenceError because `console` is a DOM API object and is not defined in the NodeJS runtime environment
It executes successfully because the NodeJS API includes its own implementation of `console.log` that outputs to the terminal
It silently discards the output because NodeJS is designed for server use and does not support any form of console printing

questions.explanationMd: NodeJS provides a `console` API, and `console.log()` writes output to the terminal or standard output.

questions.questionMd: The Internet was originally developed in 1969 by which organization to connect computers at research facilities and universities?

options.text: Transmission Control Protocol Institute (TCPI)
Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA)
European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN)
World Wide Web Consortium (W3C)

questions.explanationMd: The early Internet grew from ARPANET, a DARPA-funded project connecting research institutions.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what is the default port number used for HTTP requests when no port is specified in a URL?

options.text: Port 443, which is commonly reserved for encrypted HTTPS communication between browsers and remote web servers
Port 80, which is the well-known default port for Hypertext Transfer Protocol traffic on the World Wide Web
Port 53, which is assigned to the Domain Name System service for resolving hostnames to IP addresses
Port 3000, which is the standard development port used by NodeJS and ExpressJS applications running locally

questions.explanationMd: HTTP uses port 80 by default when no explicit port is included in the URL.

questions.questionMd: When is the `request` event emitted on a NodeJS HTTP server?

options.text: Whenever the operating system sends a DNS resolution result back to the server process running on the machine
Only once, when the server first successfully binds to the specified port and begins accepting connections
After the server finishes sending an HTTP response and closes the TCP connection with the requesting client
Each time a new HTTP request arrives for the NodeJS program to process

questions.explanationMd: A NodeJS HTTP server emits a `request` event whenever an incoming HTTP request is received.

questions.questionMd: When constructing a URL with multiple query parameters, which character is used to separate each parameter after the first one?
questions.explanationMd: In query strings, `?` starts the query section and `&` separates additional key-value parameters.

questions.questionMd: How does JavaScript read the current text entered by a user in an `<input type="text">` element?

options.text: By listening to the `input` event and reading `event.key`
By calling `getAttribute('text')` on the input element
By accessing the `.value` property of the input element
By reading the `.textContent` property of the input element

questions.explanationMd: For text inputs, the live user-entered value is accessed with the element's `.value` property.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what is the JavaScript coding convention for indicating that a method is intended to be private?

options.text: Using the `private` keyword before the method definition
Declaring the method with `const` instead of inside the class body
Wrapping the method body inside a closure immediately
Prefixing the method name with an underscore, e.g. `_methodName()`

questions.explanationMd: A leading underscore is a common convention indicating a method or property is intended for internal/private use.

questions.questionMd: When using the concise arrow function syntax, under what conditions can you omit the curly braces and the `return` keyword?

options.text: When the function body contains only a single return statement
When the function is defined inside a class constructor
When the function takes more than two parameters
When the function is assigned to a variable declared with `var`

questions.explanationMd: Concise arrow functions allow implicit return when the body is a single expression.

questions.questionMd: What does JSON stand for?

options.text: JavaScript Object Notation
JavaScript Ordered Node
JavaScript Syntax Object Notation
Java Serialized Object Network

questions.explanationMd: JSON stands for JavaScript Object Notation.

questions.questionMd: According to the course evaluation structure, what percentage of the final grade is determined by the midterm component?
questions.explanationMd: The course evaluation structure marks the midterm component as 40% of the final grade.

questions.questionMd: When a method like `_onJsonReady` is passed as a callback to `.then()`, why must it be bound using `this._onJsonReady = this._onJsonReady.bind(this)` in the constructor?

options.text: To prevent the method from being called more than once
To allow the method to accept multiple parameters from the Promise chain
To ensure that `this` inside the callback correctly refers to the class instance
To make the method execute synchronously instead of asynchronously

questions.explanationMd: Binding fixes the callback's `this` value so it still refers to the class instance when the method is invoked by the Promise chain.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what is an important limitation of the CustomEvent API in JavaScript?

options.text: CustomEvents can only be dispatched and listened to on HTML elements
CustomEvents can only be created inside ES6 class constructors
CustomEvents cannot carry any additional data in their event object
CustomEvents are not supported in any browser that uses the V8 engine

questions.explanationMd: The lecture highlights that CustomEvents are tied to DOM elements/EventTarget-style usage rather than arbitrary class-instance communication.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture summary, what is the correct sequence of steps that occurs when you navigate to a URL in your browser?

options.text: The browser binds to a local port, then calls `http.createServer()` to intercept the server's response before rendering it
The browser creates an HTTP GET request, then the operating system sends that request to the server over TCP
The operating system sends a DNS query, then the browser directly opens a socket to the resolved IP address and fetches the page
The browser parses the HTML response first, then sends an HTTP GET request to download any external CSS and JavaScript files

questions.explanationMd: At a high level, browser navigation creates an HTTP GET request and the operating system/network stack sends it to the remote server over TCP.

questions.questionMd: In the lecture's chained fetch example, what is the correct order of asynchronous operations?

options.text: `fetch` and `response.text()` run simultaneously before any handlers fire
`response.text()` runs before fetch completes
`onStreamProcessed` runs first, then fetch completes, then `onResponse` runs
fetch completes, then `onResponse` runs, then `onStreamProcessed` runs

questions.explanationMd: The `fetch()` Promise resolves first with a response, `onResponse` runs, and then the Promise returned by `response.text()` resolves so the stream/text-processing handler runs.

questions.questionMd: Why do all third-party REST APIs configure their servers to allow cross-origin `fetch()` requests?

options.text: Because without that server-side configuration, browsers would block cross-origin `fetch()` calls and external developers would not be able to access the API at all
Because browser vendors require all commercial APIs to register their domains in a public CORS whitelist maintained by the W3C before allowing cross-origin access
Because configuring CORS on the server encrypts all cross-origin traffic using TLS, which protects API keys transmitted in request headers from being intercepted
Because CORS configuration is mandated by the HTTP/2 specification for any server that handles more than a certain number of simultaneous connections per second

questions.explanationMd: Browsers enforce CORS, so public APIs must send appropriate CORS headers if browser-based clients from other origins should access them.

questions.questionMd: What content type does `res.send()` use by default when sending an HTTP response in ExpressJS?

options.text: `text/html`, which treats the response body as an HTML document by default
`text/plain`, which sends the response as unformatted plain text without any HTML markup or content-type negotiation
`application/octet-stream`, which sends the response as raw binary data with no assumed encoding or character set
`application/json`, which serializes JavaScript objects into JSON format before transmitting them to the client browser

questions.explanationMd: In the lecture example, `res.send()` is treated as sending HTML/text content suitable for browser rendering by default.

questions.questionMd: What is npm primarily used for in a NodeJS development workflow?

options.text: It is a version control system integrated with NodeJS that tracks changes to JavaScript source files across a development team
It is a built-in NodeJS module that provides methods for creating HTTP servers and handling incoming TCP connections
It is a command-line tool that installs packages (libraries and tools) written in JavaScript and compatible with NodeJS
It is a browser extension that allows developers to inspect and modify the DOM of pages served from a NodeJS backend

questions.explanationMd: npm is the Node package manager; it installs and manages JavaScript packages used in NodeJS projects.

questions.questionMd: In REST API terminology, what is the “base URL”?

options.text: The fallback URL used when the primary endpoint is unavailable
The root address of the API server to which all endpoint paths are appended
The full URL including all query parameters for a specific request
The URL of the web page that consumes the API

questions.explanationMd: The base URL is the common root address of an API; specific endpoint paths are appended to it.

questions.questionMd: In the URL `http://www.example.com:8080`, what does the value `8080` represent?

options.text: The TCP port on which the HTTP server is listening
The subnet mask of the server's IP address
The version number of the HTTP protocol being used
The number of packets sent in the HTTP request

questions.explanationMd: A number after the hostname and colon in a URL specifies the port used to contact the server.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what type of HTTP request does a browser issue when you load a URL by typing it into the address bar?

options.text: An HTTP POST request, because navigation events send the current page's form state to the server as part of the browser's session continuity mechanism
An HTTP OPTIONS request, so that the browser can first discover which methods and content types the destination server supports before committing to a full request
An HTTP HEAD request that retrieves only the response headers so the browser can determine the content type and size before deciding to download the full body
An HTTP GET request for the resource at that URL

questions.explanationMd: Typing a URL into the address bar causes the browser to request the resource with HTTP GET.

questions.questionMd: In a chained Promise pattern, what must `onResponse` return for the next `.then()` in the chain to receive the text data?

options.text: The response object itself
A resolved string from `response.status`
A JSON object created with `JSON.parse()`
The Promise returned by `response.text()`

questions.explanationMd: Returning `response.text()` passes its resulting Promise into the chain; the next `.then()` receives the resolved text value.

questions.questionMd: If a page at `abc.com/users` makes a `fetch()` request to `abc.com/search`, how is this request classified according to CORS rules?

options.text: It is a same-origin request because both URLs share the same domain
It is a cross-origin request because the URL paths `/users` and `/search` are different, which triggers the browser's preflight OPTIONS mechanism
It is classified as a restricted request because it travels between two different endpoints on the server, which requires an explicit Access-Control-Allow-Path header
It is a cross-origin request because `fetch()` always performs an origin check against the `window.location.href` value at the time the call is initiated

questions.explanationMd: CORS origin is based on scheme, host, and port, not the URL path. Two paths under the same origin are same-origin requests.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what is the recommended way to send data in a POST request rather than using query parameters in the URL?

options.text: Append data to the URL path as route segments instead of query parameters so Express can read them from `req.params`
Send the data in the body of the HTTP request rather than appending it as query parameters to the URL
Encode all data as Base64 and place it in the Authorization header so the server can decode it securely upon receipt
Store data in the browser's local storage before making the POST request so the server can retrieve it on the next GET request

questions.explanationMd: POST requests commonly send submitted data in the HTTP request body instead of exposing it as URL query parameters.

questions.questionMd: Who created JSON according to the lecture?

options.text: Ryan Dahl
Tim Berners-Lee
Douglas Crockford
Brendan Eich

questions.explanationMd: The lecture attributes JSON to Douglas Crockford.
